1.say: Push the thin white battery wire straight down into its own 5-hole connected row at the top edge of your breadboard, and push the thin blue battery wire straight down into a different 5-hole row well apart to its right. In the video: both at the top edge of the small white breadboard, white on the left, blue on the right.
placements: thin white battery feed wire with stripped end → into its own 5-hole connected terminal row at the top edge of the breadboard, not sharing a row with the blue wire; this mini board has no marked + red / - blue rails, use the main field; in the video: top edge left side - the video doesn't show which row number; match the picture

thin blue battery feed wire with stripped end → into a different 5-hole connected terminal row at the top edge, several holes to the right of the white wire; in the video: top edge right side - the video doesn't show which row number; match the picture
watch_for: both wires in the same 5-hole connected row - the battery is shorted and the circuit cannot work; if so, pull one wire out and move it several holes away
wire pushed in only halfway with bare metal showing outside - if the LED later stays dark, push each wire straight down until seated
1.check_yourself: Both the thin white wire on the left and the thin blue wire on the right stand upright from two separate holes along the top edge of the white breadboard.
1.safety: Keep the bare ends of the white and blue wires from touching each other while the battery pack is connected so you don't short the batteries.

2.say: Lay the small blue-banded resistor with two long wire legs flat across the top of the breadboard so one leg shares the white wire's row and the other leg sits in its own separate row toward the blue wire. In the video: arched flat across the top edge, left end with the white wire.
placements: small blue-bodied 220-ohm resistor with two long bent thin wire legs → arched across the top of the breadboard with one leg in the same 5-hole row as the white wire and the other leg in a separate 5-hole row toward the blue-wire side, legs in different rows from each other; in the video: lying flat across the top - the video doesn't show which row numbers; match the picture
watch_for: both resistor legs in the same 5-hole row - the resistor is bypassed and the LED can burn out; if the LED is blinding bright, move one leg to a different row
resistor legs in rows that do not share with the white wire - the circuit is open; if the LED stays dark, reseat the end into the exact same row as the white wire
2.check_yourself: The small blue-banded resistor lies flat in an arch across the top of the white breadboard with the white wire standing at its left end.

3.say: Push the round blue LED straight down so its short leg with the flat side goes in the same row as the resistor leg farthest from the white wire, and its long leg goes in the same row as the blue wire. In the video: upright on the right side of the white breadboard, glowing blue.
placements: round blue LED with long leg anode + and short leg with flat side cathode - → upright with short leg in the same 5-hole row as the resistor leg farthest from the white wire and long leg in the same 5-hole row as the blue power wire, legs in different rows from each other; in the video: upright on the right side of the board - the video doesn't show which row; match the picture
watch_for: LED reversed with long leg toward the resistor side - if the LED stays dark, pull it and swap the two legs
both LED legs in the same 5-hole row or in rows not sharing with the resistor and blue wire - if the LED stays dark, reseat so each leg shares its intended neighbor's row
3.check_yourself: The round blue LED stands straight upright on the right side of the white breadboard glowing bright blue with the blue wire beside it.
